Resolves #19140
Refs #18985

Pins `Neo.calendar.store.Events#getDayRecords(date)` in `test/playwright/unit/calendar/EventsStore.spec.mjs`, covering single-day event selection, `startDate` ascending sort order when events are added late-first, exclusion of overnight events spanning midnight on both start and end days, exclusion of events on other days, and `[]` on empty days.

Evidence: L1 (Playwright single-thread unit test suite in Node.js) → L1 required (AC-1 through AC-5).

Micro-review eligible: test-only — adds one unit spec (`test/playwright/unit/calendar/EventsStore.spec.mjs`) covering `Neo.calendar.store.Events#getDayRecords(date)` without modifying `src/`.

### `@neo-opus-ada` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-11-05T10:23:24Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical: test-only. It adds one unit spec and changes nothing in `src/`, so it teaches no architectural concept.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** At `f3be1c6ef8` the spec pins `Neo.calendar.store.Events#getDayRecords` with one test per row of #19140's table. I checked each row against `src/calendar/store/Events.mjs:39-57`: an event counts only when `DateUtil.matchDate` holds for both its `startDate` and its `endDate`. Each assertion also discriminates. Without the `startDate` sorter (`Events.mjs:29-32`), the late-first test would read `['late', 'early']`. If the rule widened to any overlap, the overnight test would fail on both days. I looked for time-zone dependence and found none: `matchDate` (`src/util/Date.mjs:125-129`) compares local calendar fields, and the spec builds local `Date`s, so it gives the same result in any zone. Setup follows `test/playwright/unit/data/Store.spec.mjs`, `afterEach` destroys each store, and CI is green on this head (36 pass, 1 skipped).

**Findings:** None.
